exposure: Planned cesarean section (cardiac reasons vs. obstetric reasons)
Mode of delivery (elective cesarean vs. emergency cesarean)
Mode of delivery (planned cesarean section vs. planned vaginal delivery)
cohort: 1262 women with structural heart disease who delivered between January 2007 and June 2011, data from the Registry on Pregnancy and Cardiac Disease
finding: In women with structural heart disease, planned cesarean section did not demonstrate any advantage over planned vaginal delivery in terms of maternal outcome but was associated with lower gestational age and birth weight.
mod_finding: Planned cesarean section did not show a difference in maternal outcomes compared to planned vaginal delivery but was associated with lower gestational age and birth weight.
